en: The Second Part of the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga.
2.15 Section on Settling (Samathavāra) By how many of the seven methods of settling are the offenses committed by consenting to physical contact settled among the seven methods of settling?
The offenses committed by consenting to physical contact are settled by three of the seven methods of settling.

It may be settled by both *sammukhāvinaya* (settlement in the presence of) and *paṭiññātakaraṇa* (acting according to what has been admitted); it may be settled by both *sammukhāvinaya* and *tiṇavatthāraka* (covering over as with grass)… [and so on].

Regarding the offenses committed due to requesting and eating curd, by how many of the seven principles for settling disputes (*samatha*) are these offenses settled among the seven principles for settling disputes?
The offenses committed due to requesting and eating curd are settled by three of the seven principles for settling disputes.
It may be by means of both resolution face-to-face and acting according to what has been admitted; it may be by means of both resolution face-to-face and covering over as with grass.
The seventh section on the methods of settling disputes is finished.
